title: Madame Tussauds Singapore Courts Indian Travellers With Diwali Icons and a Two-for-One Deal
excerpt: The Sentosa attraction's Icons of India experience puts Deepika Padukone, Shah Rukh Khan, Varun Dhawan and Ranveer Singh at the centre of its Diwali programming, with a Buy 1 Get 1 MakeMyTrip offer for bookings from October 21 to November 15.
body:
• Madame Tussauds Singapore and MakeMyTrip have launched Icons of India, a limited-period Diwali experience built around the attraction's Indian cinema figures.
  • Visitors can pose with wax figures of Deepika Padukone, Shah Rukh Khan, Varun Dhawan and Ranveer Singh at the Sentosa attraction.
  • MakeMyTrip is offering an exclusive Buy 1 Get 1 deal on tickets for bookings made between October 21 and November 15, 2026 — the concrete saving for Indian travellers heading to Singapore over the festive season.
  • The attraction, at 40 Imbiah Road on Sentosa, is open daily; kids below 3 enter free and online bookings can be rescheduled free of charge.

Singapore is pitching directly for the Indian festive-season traveller this Diwali. Madame Tussauds Singapore has teamed up with MakeMyTrip for Icons of India, a limited-period experience that puts the attraction's Bollywood figures at the centre of its Festival of Lights programming, the two companies announced on October 19 through Media OutReach Newswire.

Guests can get up close with the wax figures of Deepika Padukone, Shah Rukh Khan, Varun Dhawan and Ranveer Singh, alongside a special lineup of Diwali activities. The commercial hook for travellers is specific: MakeMyTrip is offering an exclusive Buy 1 Get 1 deal on tickets for bookings made between October 21 and November 15, 2026.

"Travellers today want to do more than just visit a destination; they want experiences that make the trip memorable. With many Indians travelling abroad over the festive season, Icons of India gives travellers heading to Singapore one more reason to plan their trip around Diwali."

— Jasmeet Singh, Chief Business Officer – Holidays & Experiences, MakeMyTrip

Why Singapore, why Diwali

Singapore is one of the most-booked short-haul destinations for Indian families during the Diwali break, and its attractions compete hard for that window. Wade Chang, general manager of Madame Tussauds Singapore, said the campaign is built around Diwali's place in Indian culture: "Diwali is an important celebration of Indian culture, bringing people together through the shared spirit of light, joy and togetherness. Through the Icons of India campaign, we're excited to bring guests closer to the most iconic stars and create memorable experiences." MakeMyTrip's Singh added that the attraction is bookable on the platform "as easily as a hotel or a flight," which matters for families assembling a festive itinerary in one checkout.

Planning a visit

The attraction sits at 40 Imbiah Road on Sentosa Island. A standard visit bundles more than the wax figures: the ticket includes the Images of Singapore walk-through of 200 years of the city-state's history and the Spirit of Singapore boat ride, alongside zones such as the Marvel Universe 4D experience. Practical details from the official Madame Tussauds Singapore site: book online in advance to save, kids below 3 enter free, and tickets can be rescheduled free of charge — book through the tickets page or claim the Buy 1 Get 1 window on MakeMyTrip between October 21 and November 15.

The bigger play

For Singapore's attractions, Indian cinema is not decoration — it is the draw. The Icons of India campaign spotlights what both brands called the enduring global appeal of Indian cinema, and it lands in a season when Indian outbound travel peaks. For diaspora families routing a Diwali trip through Singapore — or Singapore-based Indian families hosting visiting relatives — a Bollywood-fronted attraction with a two-for-one ticket window is a straightforward add to the itinerary.
